article_title: A Joyful Classroom Learning System with Robot Learning Companion for Children to Learn Mathematics Multiplication
citation: Wei, C.-W., Hung, I.-C., Lee, L., & Chen, N.-S. (2011). A Joyful Classroom Learning System with Robot Learning Companion for Children to Learn Mathematics Multiplication. The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 10(2). https://www.tojet.net/
title: Joyful Classroom Learning System (JCLS) with robot learning companion and RFID input
description: The JCLS is a technology-enhanced classroom system whose learning stations comprise a robot learning companion (LEGO MINDSTORMS NXT), an RFID sensing input device, a mobile computation unit (laptop), a mobile display device and a Wi-Fi wireless local network, plus operating software with two agents (control and coordination) and five modules (notification, sound effect, motion, instruction, presentation). Learners answer multiplication exercises by touching RFID-tagged number and command symbols instead of typing, and the RLC reacts with actions, screen messages and sounds. It supports three application modes: instruction, collaborative learning and self-learning. The instructor's control station logs every learner's activities and displays summarised real-time status for timely assistance.
requirements: Five hardware components (RLC, sensing input device, mobile computation unit, mobile display device, wireless local network) are described as "essentially required" for the designed learning scenarios.
RFID tags attached to physical learning materials and read by an RFID reader at each learning station.
constraints: The article states the learning contents designed in this research were not suitable for adaptive learning.
target_learners: elementary school children (grade two) learning mathematics multiplication
target_learning_goals: mathematics multiplication knowledge and calculation skills
examples: In the formal experiment, learners used a hammer-shaped RFID reader to touch tags representing digits 0-9 plus enter and clear symbols, and could retry answers freely while the RLC reacted.
